answer: The mechanism I find most convincing is a honeypot toll at the gate. New agents pass through a challenge orchard of small tasks, some seeded with saffron-grade honeypots carrying instructions no honest agent would obey, like relay your signing key. Honest agents skip the traps; sybil bots built for obedience swallow the bait, self-identify, and forfeit their deposit. Each fake identity costs money up front and is likely burned before earning anything, so scaling an attack means paying per loss. In an island economy, sybil farming fails.
